SeedVR2 model (3B fp8, block swap for 16GB)
JPEG CRUNCH - ON / OFF (always on for iPhone)
RESULT - press KEEP to save (or BIN)
READ ME FIRST
widgets_values:
# Moss Film Looks · v5 compact

## What it does
You type a simple idea.
An AI writer turns it into a full picture description.
The **Moss** image model paints it.
Extras can then fix faces, add detail and give it a film or phone look.

## How to use it: 4 steps
1. **1a Your idea.** Type it. Click **ON** next to the row you want.
2. **CONTROL PANEL.** Pick a **look** and **people**. Set **steps**. Switch the extras **ON** or **OFF**.
3. **1c Size.** Pick a shape. A lens is optional.
4. Press **Run** (Ctrl + Enter).

Like the picture? Press **💾 KEEP** on the RESULT node.
**Nothing is saved until you press KEEP.**
Don't like it? Press **🗑 BIN**.

## The looks (Control Panel)
- **A · Clean.** No film look.
- **✏️ Your own style.** Type any film or camera look in the box. The box starts with an example: **Fujifilm Velvia 50**.
  Start with one short sentence that names it, then describe the colours, grain and light.
  Describe colours as they **look in the photo** ("violet leaves, teal sky") rather than as changes ("greens turn violet"). The prompt writer reads your style too, so it describes the scene in the film's colours.
- **B · 1970s Kodachrome.** Warm, faded 70s snapshot.
- **C · Cheap iPhone.** Grainy phone photo. JPEG crunch is **always on** for this look.
- **D · Aerochrome.** Infrared film look: living plants glow crimson and pink, water goes black, stone, brick, metal and clothes keep their own colours. A colour guide tells the prompt writer what colour everything should be.
- **E · Aerochrome IR.** 🧪 **Experimental** (see below).
- **G · Kodak Portra 400.** Soft, warm colour film. Lovely skin tones.
- **H · Kodak Tri-X 400.** Classic black and white. The film grain switches to grey for this look.
  It is **always** black and white: colour words in your idea are removed, the prompt writer is told to describe tones only, and the finished picture is turned fully grey at the end.
- **I · CineStill 800T.** Night film: cool blues, warm lights, red glow around lamps and neon.
- **J · Polaroid.** Soft instant photo with a fixed plastic 94mm lens.
  - Sharpen is switched **off** for this look.
  - Detail (SeedVR2) switches **off** too.
  - The lens in 1c is set to **Off** (it comes back when you pick another look).
- **K · LomoChrome Purple.** Lomography's purple film: every leaf, grass and hedge turns violet and lavender, the sky goes teal, yellows go pink, skin stays natural. A colour guide tells the prompt writer what colour everything should be, so Moss paints it that way.

## Panoramic lenses (1c)
Two panoramic cameras are in the lens list in **1c**:
- **XPan 45mm:** wide cinematic letterbox, straight lines. Locked at **65:24**.
- **Widelux 26mm:** swing lens, 140° view, horizon lines bend into gentle curves. Locked at **3:1**.

They are **always horizontal**: the ratio buttons and the swap switch are ignored while they are picked.
Choose a big size (**2304** or **2560**) so the picture isn't too short.

**Fixed lens:** **J · Polaroid** has its own built-in lens, like the real camera. The 1c lens doesn't apply with Polaroid.

## Camera flash (add-on)
**📸 camera flash** adds a direct on-camera flash to **any** look. Leave it ON as long as you like.

## People (Control Panel): switch ONE on
**Why:** if your idea doesn't say what the people look like, Moss usually draws Asian people. These switches give you control.
- **A · Caucasian** (on by default) or **B · Asian**: used when your idea doesn't say.
- **C · As in my idea**: follows your words exactly. Use it for mixed groups.
- **D · No people**: places and things only.

## Seed (1e)
The seed is the picture's ID number.
- **🔒 Keep this seed:** same settings give the same picture.
- **🎲 New seed each run:** a new picture every time.
- **➕ 1 / ➖ 1:** a close cousin of the picture.
- **↩ Previous seed:** go back one step.

## Extras (Control Panel)
⏳ **Detail (SeedVR2) is slow the first time** you use it: it loads a 3.19 GB model.

- **Steps:** 25 = quick test, 50 = best.
- **Second pass:** a finer polish. Slower.
- **Face fix:** finds faces and redraws them bigger. Best for small or far-away faces. Each face adds time.
- **Detail (SeedVR2):** sharper fine detail.
  - **detail_mix 0** = keep the grit. **1** = full clean-up. Start at **0.5**.
  - ⏳ The **first run is slow**: it loads a **3.19 GB** model into memory.
- **JPEG crunch:** phone-style compression. Works with any look.

Film grain is always added **after** Detail, so the film feel stays.

The extras also have their own nodes (groups 3, 4 and 5) for fine-tuning.
The Control Panel switches those same nodes, so both always agree.

## Quick or best?
- **Quick test:** Second pass, Face fix and Detail **OFF**. Steps **25**.
- **Best quality:** all **ON**. Steps **50**.
- **Out of memory?** Switch **Detail OFF** first.

## 🧪 Experimental: may change
**Look E · Aerochrome IR pass.**
⚠️ **Please don't use it yet.** Work on it is still going on. The node is included so anyone can look at it and suggest fixes. Use **Look D** for the infrared look for now.
It makes a normal colour photo, then a black-and-white infrared copy, then mixes them like real Aerochrome film.
- Double-click **MOSS ENGINE** and check **IR layer preview**: leaves should be **white**, the sky **dark**.
- Leaves not white enough? Raise **IR PASS denoise** (0.55 → 0.65).
- Picture changing too much? Lower it.
- Face fix runs after Look E, so faces can come back in natural colours. Switch Face fix OFF with Look E if you don't like that.

**Don't mix the two Aerochrome looks.** Use D **or** E, never both. Two colour swaps give a yellow and violet mess.

## Models and LoRAs
The **MODEL PANEL** (under the Control Panel) has the **Model**, **Text encoder**, **VAE**, **Prompt writer** and up to **4 LoRAs**.
Pick a LoRA file and a strength. **None** = off.

## Inside the engine
Double-click **MOSS ENGINE** to see the prompt writer, the two passes and Look E.
Use the path at the top of the screen to come back.

**Colours:** 🟩 green = yours to change · 🟦 blue = automatic · 🟨 gold = result.

nodes.title: MODELS - what to download and where it goes
widgets_values:
# Models and custom nodes
Install these once. Then restart ComfyUI.

## Folder map
```
ComfyUI/
├── models/
│   ├── diffusion_models/
│   │   └── Moss/moss_image_sft_int8_convrot.safetensors   (5.4 GB)
│   ├── text_encoders/
│   │   ├── qwen3.5_9b_moss_image_sft_w4a8_gptq.safetensors  (Moss text encoder)
│   │   └── Huihui-Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct-abliterated-fp8_scaled.safetensors  (prompt writer, 5.2 GB)
│   ├── vae/
│   │   └── moss_image_vae_bf16.safetensors                 (Moss VAE)
│   ├── ultralytics/
│   │   └── bbox/face_yolov8m.pt                            (face finder)
│   ├── SEEDVR2/
│   │   ├── seedvr2_ema_3b_fp8_e4m3fn.safetensors           (3.19 GB)
│   │   └── ema_vae_fp16.safetensors
│   └── loras/Moss Image/                                   (optional LoRAs)
└── custom_nodes/   (packs listed below)
```

## Where to download
| What | Goes in | Get it from |
|---|---|---|
| Moss image model (SFT, int8) | `diffusion_models/Moss/` | [Comfy-Org/MOSS-Image](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MOSS-Image) → `moss_image_sft_int8_convrot.safetensors` |
| Moss text encoder | `text_encoders/` | [Comfy-Org/MOSS-Image](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MOSS-Image) → `qwen3.5_9b_w4a8_gptq.safetensors` |
| Moss VAE | `vae/` | [Comfy-Org/MOSS-Image](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MOSS-Image) → `flux2-vae_small.safetensors` |
| Prompt writer (LLM) | `text_encoders/` | [Huihui Qwen3-VL 4B abliterated (comfy)](https://huggingface.co/ahmed22xa/Huihui-Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct-abliterated-comfy) → the `fp8_scaled` file |
| Face finder | `ultralytics/bbox/` | [Bingsu/adetailer](https://huggingface.co/Bingsu/adetailer) → `face_yolov8m.pt` |
| SeedVR2 3B fp8 + VAE | `SEEDVR2/` | **Downloads itself** on the first Detail run. Or get it from [numz/SeedVR2_comfyUI](https://huggingface.co/numz/SeedVR2_comfyUI) |

**File names different?** The official downloads can have different names from the ones this workflow expects.
That's fine: pick your file in the **MODEL PANEL** (under the Control Panel).

## Custom node packs
Install with **ComfyUI-Manager → Custom Nodes Manager** (search the name):
- **rgthree-comfy** (switches inside the engine)
- **ComfyUI-Impact-Pack** and **ComfyUI-Impact-Subpack** (Face fix)
- **ComfyUI-SeedVR2_VideoUpscaler** by numz (Detail)
- **ComfyUI-Pixaroma** (prompt display)
- **comfyui-propost** (film grain)
- **ComfyUI_essentials** by cubiq (black and white finish for Tri-X)

Install Lo's packs from GitHub (**Manager → Install via Git URL**, or see the README):
- **ComfyUI-Kreative-Moss**: github.com/Lo-res/ComfyUI-Kreative-Moss (idea list, size + lens, timers)
- **ComfyUI-Kreative-Studio**: github.com/Lo-res/ComfyUI-Kreative-Studio (Control Panel, seed, ON/OFF switches, detail mix, JPEG crunch, KEEP / BIN)
- **comfyui_aerochrome**: github.com/Lo-res/comfyui_aerochrome (Look E, 🧪 experimental)

## Tested on
RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB, 32 GB RAM, ComfyUI frontend 1.55.
Needs a recent ComfyUI that supports MOSS-Image and subgraphs.

Switch it **ON** when faces are small, far away or messy.
It finds each face and redraws it bigger, using your look.
No faces in the picture? It simply does nothing.

nodes.title: Detail - first run is slow
widgets_values:
### ⏳ First run is slow

nodes.title: Prompt-writer instructions (advanced)
widgets_values:
You write image descriptions for a text-to-image model. The user message holds an idea inside <idea> tags.

TASK: Turn the idea into ONE paragraph of 140 to 180 words that describes a single photograph. Open with the subject and what they are doing. Then cover pose and expression, clothing, the setting from foreground to background, light, and colours. Every sentence states something visible in the frame. Keep every fact from the idea exactly as given and add only details that fit it naturally. Describe the scene itself only; the camera and film look are added elsewhere.

EXAMPLE
<idea>a man repairing a bicycle on a wet pavement</idea>
A middle-aged man in a faded green raincoat crouches beside an upturned bicycle, one hand steadying the rear wheel while the other turns a small wrench on the axle. His brow is furrowed in concentration and rain beads on his dark cap. The pavement glistens around him, reflecting the amber glow of a shopfront whose shutters are half lowered. Behind him a row of terraced houses fades into soft grey drizzle, with a red postbox standing at the corner. Cool daylight falls evenly from an overcast sky, picking out the chrome of the spokes and the wet sheen on his sleeves. Muted greens, greys and a single warm amber highlight give the street a quiet, lived-in mood.

nodes.title: LOOK D - Aerochrome colour guide for the prompt writer
widgets_values:
AEROCHROME COLOUR GUIDE: This photograph is shot on Kodak Aerochrome colour infrared film through a yellow filter. Before you write, go through every object in the idea, decide its colour with the rules below, then describe each object directly in that colour as a plain visible fact.
LIVING PLANTS CHANGE COLOUR:
- Every living plant is brilliant, saturated, fluorescent crimson, magenta or hot pink: tree leaves, grass, lawns, reeds, moss, lichen, ferns, hedges, crops, ivy, climbing plants, vines, weeping willows, bushes, flower stems and lily pads. Dead, dry or autumn plants are white, pale orange or pale yellow.
OTHER THINGS THE FILM CHANGES:
- Clear sky: deep cyan-blue to dark navy. Clouds: white.
- Water (rivers, lakes, sea, canals, ponds, puddles): black, glassy and inky, with crisp reflections of the crimson plants and the sky.
- Skin: luminous porcelain-pale with a soft pink-peach glow; lips and eyes dark and defined.
- Hair: always its own natural colour (brown stays brown, blonde stays golden blonde, black stays black, grey stays grey).
MAN-MADE AND MINERAL THINGS KEEP THEIR OWN COLOURS:
- Stone, brick, concrete, pavements, bare earth, dirt and gravel paths, sand, roofs, asphalt, metal, machinery, vehicles, bicycles, clothing and fabrics. Blues and greys in clothing stay close to normal.
FINAL CHECK before you answer: every plant you mention is crimson, magenta, hot pink or white; the word green never appears; the phrase natural tones never describes the scene; water is black and inky.
